issues.legal_issue: Uncovered raised platforms and masonry platforms on village-site land, including land used as a bazaar, qualify as buildings for settlement with the outgoing proprietor together with their appurtenant land.
material_facts: The outgoing proprietor owned the open ottas and chabutras on land used for a bazaar within the village site.
The settlement authorities had settled land under structures carrying sheds with the proprietor but had not settled land under the uncovered structures.
The dispute concerned whether the uncovered structures and their appurtenant land were eligible for settlement under the statutory abolition scheme.
issues.conclusion: The uncovered ottas and chabutras were buildings within the meaning of section 5(a), and the land covered by them together with appurtenant land had to be settled with the outgoing proprietor. The fact that the structures stood on land used as a bazaar did not exclude them from the village-site exception.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4(1)(a) and 5(a) of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950, village-site land generally vested in the State, but land on which a qualifying building belonging to the outgoing proprietor stood, together with appurtenant land, was to be settled with that proprietor. A bazaar within the village abadi remained part of the village site for this purpose. In this statutory context, “building” bears its literal meaning of something built; it need not have walls and a roof. Moir v. Williams, Morrison v. Commissioners of Inland Revenue, and Samuel Small v. Parkway Auto Supplies were distinguished because the meaning of “building” depends on the enactment and context in which it is used.

rule.if: abolition_settlement_proceeding and outgoing_proprietor_owns_structure and structure_is_built_on_village_site_including_bazaar_area and structure_is_uncovered_platform

predicates.abolition_settlement_proceeding: The dispute arises in a proceeding to settle land following abolition of proprietary rights.
predicates.outgoing_proprietor_owns_structure: The outgoing proprietor owns the structure on the land.
predicates.structure_is_built_on_village_site_inclu: The structure stands on land within the village site, which may include land used as a bazaar.
predicates.structure_is_uncovered_platform: The structure is an uncovered raised platform or similar built structure.

issues.definition: When an outgoing proprietor owns an uncovered platform built on village-site land, including bazaar land, the land beneath it and its appurtenant land are settleable with that proprietor.

issues.legal_issue: A concession on a contextual issue that is not purely a question of law cannot be withdrawn by a party on appeal.
material_facts: The State’s counsel had not challenged in the High Court the interpretation that the term “buildings” included the structures at issue.
The State later sought to withdraw that concession and argue that the structures were not buildings.
The Court considered whether the issue was purely one of law and held that it was not.
issues.conclusion: The State was not entitled to withdraw the concession because the issue whether the structures were buildings was not purely a question of law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the meaning of “buildings” in its statutory context as an issue that was not purely legal; accordingly, the State could not withdraw its concession on that issue. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is an appeal from a lower court’s decision.
predicates.party_made_prior_concession: A party’s counsel previously accepted a position before the lower court.
predicates.concession_concerns_contextual_issue_not: The accepted position concerns an issue whose resolution depends on context and is not purely a question of law.

issues.definition: In an appeal, a party cannot withdraw its earlier concession when that concession concerns a contextual issue that is not purely legal.

issues.legal_issue: Settlement must be confined to the land covered by the qualifying structures and their appurtenant land, with the precise extent determined in settlement proceedings.
material_facts: The High Court directed settlement of the entire parcel, although the area said to be covered by the structures and appurtenant land was smaller.
The proprietor’s counsel conceded that the entire parcel was not sought and that only the land covered by the structures and appurtenant land was claimed.
The precise area covered by the structures and appurtenant land was to be determined in settlement proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The direction to settle the entire parcel was modified. The State was directed to settle the land covered by the structures and their appurtenant land, with the precise area left to be determined by the revenue authorities in the settlement proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(a) provides for settlement of the land on which qualifying buildings stand and the land appurtenant to them. The precise area must be determined in the settlement proceedings; the provision does not justify directing settlement of a larger parcel beyond that land.

rule.if: abolition_settlement_appeal and lower_court_ordered_entire_parcel and entitlement_is_limited_to_structure_and_appurtenant_land and precise_extent_requires_determination

predicates.abolition_settlement_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning land settlement following abolition of proprietary rights.
predicates.lower_court_ordered_entire_parcel: The lower court directed settlement of the entire parcel.
predicates.entitlement_is_limited_to_structure_and_: The claimed settlement entitlement extends only to land covered by qualifying structures and land appurtenant to them.
predicates.precise_extent_requires_determination: The precise extent of the qualifying land has not been established and requires determination in settlement proceedings.

issues.definition: When the lower court orders settlement of an entire parcel but the entitlement covers only land beneath qualifying structures and appurtenant land, settlement is confined to that qualifying land and its precise extent is determined in settlement proceedings.
